claims.text: The as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy contains dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Internal lamellar-colony boundaries act as microcrack-nucleation sites during room-temperature deformation.
A trace boron addition will preferentially segregate to lamellar-colony boundaries.
Boron segregation will enhance cohesion at internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
Boron segregation lowers the free energy of the high-energy interphase boundaries.
Greater interfacial cohesion reduces stress concentration during tensile loading.
Reduced interfacial stress concentration delays microcrack nucleation.
Delayed microcrack nucleation permits more uniform plastic deformation.
An optimized trace boron addition will increase room-temperature yield strength relative to the boron-free baseline.
An optimized trace boron addition will increase room-temperature elongation to failure relative to the boron-free baseline.
The beneficial effect requires retention of the dual-phase lamellar microstructure, including approximately unchanged lamellar spacing and phase volume fractions.
Excessive boron can form brittle boride phases.
Brittle boride formation can degrade strength or tensile ductility.
Too little boron may provide insufficient interfacial strengthening.
The predicted benefit is bounded to ambient-temperature tensile loading and may not extend to other temperatures or loading modes.
The boron concentration that maximizes interfacial strengthening without producing harmful secondary phases is not known.
The stability of boron-enriched interfaces under cyclic or complex loading has not been established.
